decision: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Thirty-eight lines of attack were run and one produced a defect. Every load-bearing claim was re-derived from primary bytes rather than read back from the draft: both Stage A digests and both verdicts from the reviews' own count fields; all nine Claude identifiers in order with their sorted member sets, and the observations / observationsNotFindings shape on both reviews; the Codex empty-list negatives; HEAD, the D-301 adoption commit, the COORD heading tail, and the live COORD and file-08 digests; the DR-G21 OPEN token and the condition 2 and condition 4 figures at file 08 lines 357, 415 and 417; all four platform copies enumerated from disk with their digests, modes, filenames and directory count, plus the absence of a fifth entry and of any Windows directory; the equality of each copy to the D-301 payload and the unmoved state of fixtures/g21.v11/; the ordered-equal G10 and G23 platform arrays and the missing platforms key on G21 occupancy v4; the v12 and v13 Stage A verdicts, the Codex v12 finding proved unlabeled by an empty findingIdentifiers and proved to be on basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.role by its own where list, and CLAUDE-G21FXV13-S-1 proved SHOULD-FIX by its severity field; the branch endpoints against the D-236 and D-272 exclusions; and D-294 Decision 3 currency for both cross-lineage citations, confirming g21 leftover-join.v13 and anti-lockstep-leftover-join.v3 are each the latest in their lineage. Four candidate defects were pursued to source and killed on measured evidence: the 'its findings landed' plural, defeated by the register's own adopted usage at D-296 through D-301 including a one-finding instance at D-299; the continuity verb on fixtures/g21.v12/, which unlike the D-301 case names a directory that genuinely predates the artifact; the missing v11 currency-demotion clause, which the draft's scoping of v11's record to 'payload authoring' already closes; and the weak DR-102 line, which the prompt mandated in that form and which D-301 omitted entirely. The surviving defect is CLAUDE-D302-S-1: the Subject paragraph records four freeze-era fixture copies without naming D-293 Decision 8, the fixture-authoring delegation that names G21, that the subject artifact pins with its adoption commit, and that D-296 through D-301 each carry in the same position. This is the first entry to bring those four files onto the record, so it is the entry where the authority most needs to be stated.
decisionRule: CONSENT only if 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. One SHOULD-FIX stands, therefore OBJECT.

shouldFix.title: The Subject paragraph omits the D-293 Decision 8 authoring warrant that the subject artifact pins and that every sibling entry in this series records, so the entry that first puts four freeze-era fixture files on the record does not state the authority for authoring them.
shouldFix.claimUnderReview: The Subject paragraph describes the four per-D-002-platform copies, their paths, their digests and their platform provenance, but names no warrant. The only occurrence of D-293 in the draft is inside the Reversibility list's 'does not unwrite' enumeration, which records a non-effect rather than an authority.
primaryEvidence: The subject artifact pins the warrant expressly: g21-fixture-corpus.v14.json authorityClaim reads 'The warrant is D-293 Decision 8 (adoption commit c10319d207cb90e2bf9df4c5e5997cfd35a30193).' The draft records this artifact but drops the pin.

D-293's own enumeration item 8 is '**D1 (fixture authoring).** Delegated to the orchestrator under D-000 review for the enumerated G15, G16, G18, G19, G20, G21, G24-G30, OBL-HOSTILE-GOLDENS and the two DR-122 SARIF fixture obligations'. G21 is named in the delegated set, so Decision 8 is the operative authority for exactly this act.

Every entry in the current fixture-authoring series carries the pin in its Subject paragraph: D-296, D-297, D-298, D-299, D-300 and D-301 each contain the literal phrase 'authored under D-293 Decision 8'. D-302 contains no occurrence of it; grep over the draft returns D-293 only at line 79.

The four copy files at docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g21.v12/ have never been recorded by any prior COORD entry. D-301 recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v11, whose fixture is the flat file at fixtures/g21.v11/ with no platform subdirectory; the g21.v12 copies were authored at the rejected, unrecorded corpus v12. D-302 is therefore the first entry to bring these four authored files onto the record, which is the point at which the authorizing delegation most needs to be stated.

The register treats a missing load-bearing authority pin as a SHOULD-FIX in this same series: sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v1 drew a Codex SHOULD-FIX titled 'The load-bearing section 7.1 RunId park is outside the candidate's pinned input closure', recorded at D-297 as the 'unlabeled SHOULD-FIX pinning IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md'.
shouldFix.impact: COORD is the durable record; the artifact is the candidate it records. A later reader auditing on what authority bytes were written under docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/ during the implementation freeze finds the warrant in the frozen artifact but not in the decision that adopted it. The omission also breaks the series' uniform provenance shape at the one entry where the files first enter the record, which weakens the audit trail that D-293 Decision 8 was built to provide.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing asserted in the draft is false, and no prohibited effect occurs. The warrant exists and is satisfied: D-293 Decision 8 names G21 in the delegated set, and the subject artifact pins it with its adoption commit. Every fixture-side fact in the Subject paragraph -- paths, filenames, digests, mode, platform provenance, the Windows exclusion -- reproduces exactly from disk. This is an incompleteness in the record's provenance limb, not corrupt authoring or a false measurement.
shouldFix.requiredRemedy: In a turn-2 draft, add the warrant to the Subject paragraph in the series' established form -- 'authored under D-293 Decision 8' -- attached to the description of the per-D-002-platform copies. Optionally carry the artifact's adoption-commit pin (c10319d207cb90e2bf9df4c5e5997cfd35a30193) as D-300 and D-301 handle it. Change nothing else; the frozen subject artifact, both Stage A reviews and all four fixture copies stay unmoved.

advisories.title: The D-247 precedent's second currency clause -- 'Do not record v7 as current copies' -- has no analogue for v11, although the subject artifact carries the corresponding demotion.
advisories.measurement: D-247, the prior copies-after-payload entry, wrote both clauses: 'Frozen v7 remains the D-245 payload subject. Do not record v7 as current copies.' D-302 writes only the first: 'Frozen g21-fixture-corpus.v11 remains the recorded D-301 payload authoring.' The subject's own doesNot list carries 'Does not record g21-fixture-corpus.v11 as current after g21-fixture-corpus.v14 is recorded.', so the artifact demotes v11 and the entry does not. Note also that v11's own doesNot demoted only the rejected folds v9 and v10 and left the recorded predecessor v8 alone, so v14 is the first fold in this lineage to demote a recorded predecessor.
advisories.whyNotAFinding: The draft states nothing false and leaves no misreading open. Scoping v11's record to 'the recorded D-301 payload authoring' is itself the distinction the second clause would draw: the record it preserves for v11 is payload authoring, which by its own terms is not the copies record, and the Decision limb separately records v14 as the copies entry. The omitted clause is a redundant guard rather than a missing one.
advisories.status: travels as honesty work; a candidate tightening for a later entry in this lineage, not a defect in D-302

advisories.measurement: File 08 line 415 records 'DR-102 SATISFIED under D-056 Class A (D-085); leftover CC-1..CC-11 execution remains at DR-G21 / condition 4'. This entry authors a CC-5 fixture, so it acts squarely on the DR-102 leftover half. The subject artifact's doesNot carries both forms -- 'Does not SATISFY DR-102.' and 'Does not reopen DR-102 SATISFIED.' -- while the draft's header carries only the first. D-243 and D-247, the earlier copies entries, both carried 'Does not reopen DR-102 SATISFIED.'
advisories.whyNotAFinding: The review prompt mandated the DR-102 non-SATISFY line in exactly the form the draft uses, and the draft complies. The line is true, if weak. The immediately preceding entry D-301 omitted DR-102 altogether and was adopted on dual CONSENT, so D-302 is strictly more protective than its own precedent rather than less. No reopening occurs or is implied anywhere in the draft.
advisories.status: travels as honesty work; a candidate strengthening for a later entry

All three are byte-verified: the four g21.v12 copies and the single g21.v11 file all hash to 67abdd721024f0ff4e0b3f4c2fc13bc5bad42d0b7851d456d88d203d15aaa450. The directory legitimately stays at its authoring version while the corpus artifact advances, which is the same pattern g20 carries at fixtures/g20.v2/.
advisories.whyNotAFinding: Every token is fully qualified -- the directories appear as complete quoted paths, the corpus appears as g21-fixture-corpus.vN throughout, and the payload is attributed to D-301 by decision id rather than by a bare version number. No bare token is ambiguous and the bare-token audit returns clean. The spread is inherent to a copies entry that follows a separate payload-authoring entry, and D-247 carried the same three-way spread.

observations.title: D-301's causal connective between the G10 quote and the missing occupancy platforms array is split into two independent assertions.
observations.measurement: D-301 wrote 'quoted from harness.DR-G10... because occupancy v4 has no platforms array'. D-302 states the quote and, in a later sentence, 'G21 occupancy v4 has no platforms array'. Both facts are present and both verify; the causal link is implicit.
